answer.diagnosis: I found no clear shortcut in the weights, though I am not certain. The trained layer-1 units form two families of radially symmetric, roughly centred filters. Large-blob units (0, 1, 8, 18, 19, 20, 22, 29) have a bright-ring detector at radius about 4–7, with a slightly negative centre and a weakly negative outer region. Small-blob units (14, 15, 23, 27) have a positive centre, a negative ring at the same radius and a positive surround. Units 2–7, 9–13, 16, 17, 21, 24–26, 28, 30 and 31 look like untrained initialisation (all values within about ±25). Layer 2 and the output combine these consistently: layer-2 units 3, 10, 12 and 14 are fed by the ring units and push the logit positive; units 1, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 13 are fed by the centre/surround units and push it negative. I checked for a localised marker: corner patches, edge rows and columns, lines or stripes. Nothing coherent appears; no corner or block has a consistent same-sign patch across units. The background shows some sparse pixels that agree across units (for example r8c2, r1c16-17, r3c12, r16c21). They are two-signed, scattered, and mostly lie at radius about 9–12, which fits an outer background-subtraction annulus plus noise fitting rather than a planted marker; a planted set of fixed pixels would look much the same, which is the main reason for my uncertainty. A background-brightness shortcut is not supported either. The positive background offset appears in a large-blob unit (8) as well as the small-blob units, so it pushes the two classes in opposite directions. It looks like a baseline or normalisation term rather than a class cue. Since the label-relevant computation appears to be ring-versus-centre/background size detection, I propose no edits.
